pairs.subject: judge-calibration-and-drift
pairs.evidence: lib/analysis/quality.ts:4 Context and repository searches found no kappa, golden-set, LLM-judge or repeatability machinery, and the inspected scoring paths calculate civic-data metrics deterministically, so LLM-judge calibration does not apply.

techniques.evidence: lib/analysis/contribution.ts:262 The contribution score is a fixed arithmetic formula; this context does not fit or select a judge against human labels.
lib/analysis/quality.ts:318 Quality aggregates mechanically derived criteria rather than measuring a judge's agreement with human quality labels.
lib/analysis/contribution-legacy.ts:76 The legacy scorer replays an earlier arithmetic formula; it does not replace a retired benchmark judge.
lib/analysis/context-provider.ts:102 The provider supplies schema descriptions as analyst context; it does not select a judging model.
lib/analysis/score-legibility.ts:188 The comparison counts parliamentary scores above a formula projection, rather than scoring candidate fidelity against reference outputs.
lib/analysis/contribution.ts:249 Component values come from deterministic activity ratios, with no stochastic judge draws whose repeatability requires measurement.
lib/analysis/context-model.ts:274 Published quality metadata carries slice criteria; there are no judge-calibration cycles requiring reserved-rubric history.
lib/analysis/atlas.ts:587 Cadence measures source-ingest freshness, rather than the age of a production judge's calibration.
lib/analysis/contribution.ts:121 The write guard checks formula-version identity; it does not authorize downstream use of LLM-judge scores.
lib/analysis/contribution-trend.ts:103 The trend compares an MP's parliamentary terms, whose activity may change, rather than monitoring quality or judge-agreement regression.
